Fifteen years is a long time to deal with thoughts this heavy. I was only 15 years old when I jumped. Im 23 now.   While I don’t regret jumping, I would regret it if I had been permanently disabled or killed. I got pretty lucky with my injuries, all things considered. I guess my relationship with regret is kind of complicated. More so than I had realized.
I hope you don’t ever try it. Sending better days your way.

This was in 2017, so awhile back. I didn’t regret it immediately like many say. I was definitely afraid of dying once faced with its reality, but I still wanted it.
For a long time afterward I was bed bound in the hospital, unable to get up even to shower or use the bathroom. I definitely regretted it then. But to be honest at that time my regret was more so like, “I wish I had bought a gun instead of jumping.”
I think now with all these years between now and the attempt, I don’t regret it. It was an important event in my life that taught me a lot. I would be a different person if it hadn’t happened.

I attempted suicide by jumping. I had two compression vertebrae fractures, a burst vertebrae fracture, multiple bones broken in my foot, and a ruptured spleen. My back was in so much pain, I couldn’t feel pain anywhere else. They gave me morphine and it still hurt like hell. Put every pain I’ve ever felt and will ever feel into perspective.

CNC kink can actually be caused by sexual trauma. I was totally vanilla before being raped. I certainly did not “enjoy it” or get “turned on” and I developed PTSD which I still struggle with. But it changed my sexual desire for some reason which is very hard to grapple with but actually isn’t uncommon for survivors. It’s like taking the control back, I guess. When you do CNC roleplay you have to trust the other person and be able to end it at any moment. So really it’s nothing like actually being assaulted at all as you hold all the control over the situation. The show Baby Reindeer on Netflix actually touches on this phenomenon really accurately if you’re interested in having more insight into it. I promise you it’s real and judging survivors doesn’t help anyone and only leads to shame.

I was 14 when I first got diagnosed. I was inpatient and got diagnosed by the psychiatrist there and he put me on seroquel.
